answer: In the Singapore Model AI Governance Framework 2nd Edition, repeatability refers to the ability to consistently perform an action or make a decision given the same scenario within one's own organization. It involves internal repetition of results. On the other hand, reproducibility refers to the ability of an independent verification team to produce the same results using the same AI method based on the documentation made by the organization. This means reproducibility involves external verification and can be seen as a broader concept that includes the ability to achieve the same results under potentially different conditions or setups.
